data.narrative:
Oxford Quantum Circuits, a Series C quantum computing company founded by Peter Leek, sits within a sector of 3 public and 8 private peers including Quantinuum, IonQ, PsiQuantum, D-Wave Quantum, and SandboxAQ. The company has raised $350M to date.

The valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, applicable given the Series C checkpoint. Using total capital raised ($350M) as a baseline proxy and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C-to-next-stage transitions yields $595M implied value. Peer-median triangulation could not be applied: while 8 quantum computing peers exist in the broader dataset, none matched narrow filters requiring same-stage, adjacent-stage, or comparable-tier comparables at the same time. A sector-wide median would introduce excessive noise given the heterogeneity of quantum approaches and commercialization timelines.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $506M (low) to $684M (high), with $595M as the point estimate. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties center on the absence of granular same-stage peer metrics and the rapid, uneven maturation across the quantum computing sector. Without comparable Series C transactions or detailed financials from peer firms, the step-up multiple carries model risk. Further narrowing of this range would require either disclosure of peer-stage capitalization events or visibility into OQC's revenue traction and technical milestones relative to the named peer set.
